title: Restriction identity via coordinate assignments
statement: Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a sign-valued Boolean function, let $J\\subseteq[n]$, let $z\\in\\{-1,1\\}^{[n]\\setminus J}$ specify the fixed signs outside $J$, and let $\\delta\\in\\mathbb R$ and $k\\in\\mathbb N$. The switching-failure probability at parameter $\\delta$ and threshold $k$ for the restriction of $f$ to $J$ equals the sum over all coordinate assignments $\\rho:[n]\\to\\{\\text{free},+1,-1\\}$ of their product weights times the indicator that the function obtained by composing the restriction specified by $(J,z)$ with $\\rho$ has decision-tree depth at least $k$. Each coordinate's weight is $\\delta$ when free and $(1-\\delta)/2$ when fixed to either sign.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the $n$-coordinate sign cube with sign-valued output
A subset $J$ of the coordinate set
